findings.message: Step 3 says "In chat or on the screen, a person accepts, approves or promotes." The product doesn't work that way. AGENTS.md rule 1 and R3 say every write goes through chat's pending-action confirm, and screens only offer an IntentButton that opens chat. The app's own suggestions page says "Decisions happen in chat." (apps/web/app/(app)/suggestions/page.tsx:35). AC-6 requires that "confirms are scoped to chat". This is the same overclaim as 062's "Each write waits for a confirm" finding. Fix: say decisions are made in chat, for example "In chat, a person accepts, approves or promotes; the screen pins the record and opens chat." Apply the same fix to the 064 mock step.
findings.scenario: A buyer reads 'on the screen', opens /suggestions or the timesheet screen, and finds no Accept or Approve control there: the page promised a feature that doesn't exist.

findings.message: The FAQ says data lives "In the region you pin for each legal entity". The product has one data region per tenant, not one per legal entity: snapshots, exports and buckets are keyed on "the tenant's data region" (docs/operations.md:9, 63-65), and nothing in packages/ ties a region to an entity. AC-6 requires claims to match the product. Fix: say "In the data region you choose for your workspace", and keep the retention and legal-hold part. Make the same change in the mock FAQ.
findings.scenario: A tenant with an AU entity and an LK entity reads that it can pin each entity to its own region, but every row and backup lands in the single tenant region.

findings.message: The play button doesn't meet AC-3. AC-3 requires a target of 64 px or more labelled "Play the 35-second product tour". The CSS makes it 56 px tall (`.m2 .play{height:56px}`) and 48 px at ≤480 px, and its accessible name is "Play the tour · 35 s, captions". The e2e test matches it with /Play the tour/, so it never checks the required label or size. Fix: set the height to at least 64 px at every breakpoint, use the AC's label (or change the AC on purpose), and assert both in marketing-video.spec.ts.
findings.scenario: At 390 px width, boundingBox() of the play button gives height 48, under the AC's 64. getByRole('button', { name: 'Play the 35-second product tour' }) finds nothing.

findings.message: When a card's action button is pressed, the button unmounts (`!done[c.id] && <button>`), and keyboard focus falls to <body>. A keyboard user loses their place in the queue. Fix: move focus to the resolved card's attribution line (tabIndex -1) or to the next card's action.
findings.scenario: Tab to 'Approve week', press Enter: document.activeElement becomes body.

findings.message: AC-7 asks for packages/ui tokens and "one button shape and one radius". The new CSS hard-codes its own palette (#6A50EE, #1D1B2E and the --g/--g2/--g3 literals) and several radii: 22, 16, 12, 11, 9, 28 and 18 px, plus var(--r). The play pill (radius 28) and the queue's .go button (11) are each a different button shape from .btn2. Fix: map these to the ui tokens, or record the exception in change.md.

change.md and the code disagree:
- The mock delta still quotes the old cast ("drafted by Git ingestion for Kasun Dias").
- It lists six bands (Delivery, People, Payroll, …), but the code renders five ("People and payroll").
- It promises seven FAQ questions, but there are six.
- The audit tiles are meant to include WCAG 2.2 AA, but no tile does.
Fix: update the doc to match what shipped, or add the missing items.

`tabIndex={0}` is set even before the tour starts. At that point `controls` is false and the Play button is the only control, so the video is a dead Tab stop: it takes focus, Space or Enter does nothing, and Play comes next. Fix: use `tabIndex={started ? 0 : -1}`. `play()` still focuses the video after `started` flips, because React applies the new tabIndex on the next commit. Another option is to focus the video in an effect after `started` becomes true.
findings.scenario: A keyboard user tabs from the hero queue before playing: focus lands on the poster video, Space does nothing, and they have to press Tab again to reach Play.

findings.message: The `.step.on` emphasis is only added by a client effect that changes the DOM of a server-rendered list. Until hydration, or if JS doesn't run, every step title renders in `--mut`, so none is emphasised and the steps read as disabled. The opposite default is safer: style `.step b` in `--ink` and dim the inactive steps only once the observer is running (for example, a class on `.how` set by the effect).
findings.scenario: The page is loaded with JS blocked or slow to hydrate: all three 'How it works' titles show muted, as if inactive.
